original_context: General topology: family 𝒩_x of neighborhoods of x such that for every neighborhood U of x there exists B∈𝒩_x with B⊆U; B need not itself be open.
definition: For a point x in a topological space X, a neighborhood basis (or fundamental system of neighborhoods) at x is a family B_x of neighborhoods of x such that every neighborhood N of x contains at least one B∈B_x.
reasoning: The independently screened locally quasi-compact-space definition requires a neighborhood basis all of whose members are quasi-compact. The abstract neighborhood-basis construction places no such restriction and should not be merged with local quasi-compactness or an open-set basis for the entire topology.

mathematical_assumptions: Every basis member is a neighborhood in the general sense: contains an open set around x, not necessarily open itself.
Every neighborhood N contains some B from the basis.
If X is nonempty, a basis at x cannot be empty.
